verses.english: Three thousand Sātāgira yakkhas, of varied hues,
possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,
came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.
These sixteen thousand yakkhas, of varied hues,
possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,
came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.
Five hundred Vessāmitta yakkhas, of varied hues,
possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,
came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.
Kumbhīra of Rājagaha — his dwelling is Mount Vepulla —
more than a hundred thousand yakkhas attend upon him —
Kumbhīra of Rājagaha, he too came to the wood, to the assembly.
And the king who rules the eastern quarter is Dhataraṭṭha,
lord of the gandhabbas, a great king of renown.

verses.pali_roman: Puttā pi tassa bahavo indanāmā mahabbalā,
verses.english: His sons too are many, all named Inda, of great strength,
possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,
came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.

verses.pali_roman: Dakkhiṇañca disaṃ rājā viruḷho tap pasāsati.
verses.english: And the king who rules the southern quarter is Viruḷha.
Lord of the kumbhaṇḍas, a great king of renown.

vocabulary.meaning: Mount Vepulla, one of the five hills ringing Rajagaha. Given here as the yakkha Kumbhira's dwelling
three of the Four Great Kings, guardians of the eastern, southern and western quarters. Kuvera of the north follows on page 321
the classes of being each Great King rules — celestial musicians, a class of dwarfish spirits, and the serpent beings
attends upon, waits on, sits close to. Used of the hundred thousand yakkhas around Kumbhira

checks.issue: THE BOOK'S BLANK LINES AND ITS BOLD DISAGREE HERE, and the blank lines were followed. 'Purimanca disam raja' is set in BOLD, which everywhere else in this section marks a new unit — but there is NO blank line before it. Measured rather than judged: rows inside this block sit 39-51px apart while every real paragraph break on the sheet is 77-113px. So verses 73-77 are ONE five-row block as printed, and the bold is recorded here instead of being turned into a break the page does not make.

THE BOOK PRINTS 'tap' WHERE THE SENSE NEEDS 'tam'. The line reads 'virulho tap pasasati' with a plain p, and page 321 prints 'kuvero tap pasasati' the same way. The same odd spelling on TWO separate sheets makes it the book's consistent reading rather than one compositor's slip, which is worth knowing before anyone corrects it. Recorded as printed, NOT corrected.

TWO COLUMNS throughout, gutter measured as a clean corridor at x 972-1188 — no ink anywhere in it over the full text height. Page 319's right column began at x 1080, so this sheet's measure is genuinely different and was not assumed from the previous page.

THE REFRAIN REPEATS VERBATIM SIX TIMES on this sheet — verses 65, 68, 71, 79, 84 are identical and so are 66, 69, 72, 80, 85. That is the book's own structure for a list of the assembled hosts, not duplication to be collapsed.
The book sets EM DASHES inside verses 73 and 74, closing a parenthetical about Kumbhira's dwelling and his retinue. Kept as printed; they are the page's punctuation and carry the sense of the aside.

Stage 1 only — this batch file is written and checked, but nothing has been written into chanting.py, because a second session is working in the same clone and holds that file. Two findings, and the first is the reason this page needed measuring twice. (1) THE BOLD AND THE BLANK LINES DISAGREE at verse 76: bold says new unit, spacing says same block, and the spacing was followed because it is what the page actually prints. A page read by eye alone would very likely have split it. (2) 'tap' FOR 'tam' AT VERSE 81, and again on page 321 — two sheets, so it is the book's reading and not a slip. The offset also steps here, 267 to 269, because IMG_0587 and IMG_0588 do not exist; the page number was read off the sheet rather than calculated, which is the standing rule and the reason this did not go wrong.
